text: Risk management is a vital process for any organization, as it helps prepare for the unexpected. The first step involves identifying potential risks, such as financial losses, operational failures, or safety hazards. Once these risks are known, teams develop mitigation strategies to reduce their likelihood or impact, perhaps by improving training or upgrading equipment. However, not all problems can be prevented, so contingency plans are created. These are clear, pre-arranged actions to take if a risk actually occurs, ensuring a swift response to limit damage. Finally, risk management is not a one-time task. It requires constant monitoring and regular reviews to spot new threats and ensure existing plans remain effective.
